title: Data migration: quality, reconciliation and rollback

videos.script: Since 1996, every litre of milk Serra Alta collects has been recorded in one program, Coleta. {{coleta}} Thirty years of farms and litres live in it, and Sebastião, who wrote it, retires in 2028. This lesson moves that data into the new farm system, and proves it arrived. {{profile}} It starts by measuring the data before anybody maps it. Farms registered twice, tax numbers left blank, one town spelled four ways. Then the mapping, field by field, and the people who sign it. {{pipeline}} Then rehearsals: the cutover night, run again and again on a copy, against the clock, until it fits. {{rehearsal}} You will read a short Python program that compares two extracts. It checks the count, the total litres and every record. You will see a target pass the first two checks and fail the third. {{reconcile}} Then the night itself. The runbook, the go or no-go, and the way back. And the moment after which going back means asking nineteen hundred farms to return their money. {{cutover}} It ends with the weeks after, when the first payment on the tenth is the real test.
